## Proof

Let $\{X_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{N}}$ be iid normal random variables (with some mean and positive variance). For each $\omega$, let $A(\omega)=\{X_t(\omega):t\in\mathbb{N}\}$ and let $\overline{A(\omega)}$ denote its closure in $\mathbb{R}$.

**Claim.** Almost surely, $A(\omega)$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$. Consequently $\overline{A(\omega)}=\mathbb{R}$ a.s., so $\ell(\overline{A(\omega)})=\ell(\mathbb{R})=+\infty\neq 0$ a.s., and therefore
$$P\bigl(\{\omega:\ell(\overline{A(\omega)})=0\}\bigr)=0.$$

**Proof of the claim.** Let $\{(p_k,q_k)\}_{k\ge 1}$ be an enumeration of all open intervals with rational endpoints; this is a countable base for the topology of $\mathbb{R}$.

Fix $k$. Since $X_t\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2)$ with $\sigma^2>0$, the distribution has full support on $\mathbb{R}$, so
$$p_k:=P\bigl(X_1\in(p_k,q_k)\bigr)=\Phi\!\left(\tfrac{q_k-\mu}{\sigma}\right)-\Phi\!\left(\tfrac{p_k-\mu}{\sigma}\right)>0.$$
By independence, the events $E_t^{(k)}:=\{X_t\in(p_k,q_k)\}$ are independent with common positive probability $p_k$. Hence
$$\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}P\bigl(E_t^{(k)}\bigr)=\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}p_k=+\infty.$$
By the second Borel–Cantelli lemma,
$$P\bigl(E_t^{(k)}\text{ i.o.}\bigr)=1,$$
i.e., almost surely infinitely many $X_t(\omega)$ fall inside $(p_k,q_k)$, so in particular $A(\omega)\cap(p_k,q_k)\neq\varnothing$ a.s.

Now define the event
$$D_k:=\bigl\{\omega:A(\omega)\cap(p_k,q_k)\neq\varnothing\bigr\},\qquad P(D_k)=1.$$
Since the topology has a countable base, $A(\omega)$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$ iff $A(\omega)$ meets every basic open interval $(p_k,q_k)$, i.e.,
$$\{\omega:A(\omega)\text{ is dense in }\mathbb{R}\}=\bigcap_{k=1}^{\infty}D_k.$$
A countable intersection of probability‑$1$ events has probability $1$, so
$$P\bigl(\{\omega:A(\omega)\text{ is dense in }\mathbb{R}\}\bigr)=1.$$

Therefore, almost surely, $\overline{A(\omega)}=\mathbb{R}$, whose Lebesgue measure is $+\infty$. The event $\{\omega:\ell(\overline{A(\omega)})=0\}$ is the complement of a probability‑$1$ event, hence has probability $0$:
$$\boxed{P\bigl(\{\omega:\ell(\overline{A(\omega)})=0\}\bigr)=0.}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
